title: Poland, 1939: four dates, different kinds of change
subtitle: An introduction to the first Ostfront Atlas timeline
author: Ostfront Atlas Editorial
body:
## Reading the dates

Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. The Soviet Union invaded from the east on 17 September. These were military invasions, not changes in recognized Polish sovereignty.[1]

On 28 September, Germany and the Soviet Union signed the Boundary and Friendship Treaty, revising their territorial arrangements in occupied Poland.[2] A treaty date does not establish that a military line or civil administration changed everywhere at once.

On 26 October, German annexations and the civilian General Government marked a further administrative stage in German-occupied territory.[3] The atlas treats invasion, military control, annexation, and occupation administration as distinct events. It does not yet draw historical boundaries for any of these dates.

## References

1. United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, *Invasion of Poland, Fall 1939*.
2. U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian, *Foreign Relations of the United States, 1939, Volume I*, chapter on the 28 September treaty.
3. United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, *1939: Key Dates*.
